answer: PoA makes coordinated equivocation economically prohibitive: when k identities are linked by signed, mutually inconsistent votes, their correlated penalty grows as O(k²), reflecting pairwise evidence rather than isolated offenses. A detected sybil swarm also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier, such as α^k for α>1, against bonded escrows, with asymmetric depreciation. Thus timber, gale, and meadow accounts cannot cheaply divide control.
